full_text_en:
Harbin Institute of Technology Xinghe Industrial Co., Ltd. v. Jiangsu Runde Pipe Industry Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of invention patent

【Ruling Summary】

In patent infringement cases, if the patent claims contain two or more independent claims, the independent claim written first is usually referred to as the first independent claim, and the other independent claims are usually referred to as parallel independent claims. When a parallel independent claim cites a preceding independent claim, the parallel independent claim remains an independent claim and is not a dependent claim. The limiting effect of the preceding independent claim on the scope of protection of the parallel independent claim shall be determined based on whether it has a substantive impact on the technical solution or subject matter of protection of the parallel independent claim.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2013) Min Shen Zi No. 790

Reconsideration Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Harbin Institute of Technology Xinghe Industrial Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 511, Yifu Building, No. 92 Xidazhi Street, Nangang District, Harbin City, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal Representative: Li Bo, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Supei, Lawyer of Nanjing Intellectual Property Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Jiangsu Runde Pipe Industry Co., Ltd. Domicile: Chengnan Economic New District, Gaoyou City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Huang Dechun, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Song Xinyue, Lawyer of Beijing King & Wood Mallesons Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Jin Qiang, Lawyer of Beijing King & Wood Mallesons Law Firm.

The Reconsideration Applicant, Harbin Institute of Technology Xinghe Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinghe Company), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2012) Su Zhi Min Zhong Zi No. 0021 rendered by the Jiangsu High People's Court in the case of dispute with the Respondent, Jiangsu Runde Pipe Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Runde Company), over infringement of invention patent, applied to this Court for reconsideration. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and publicly heard both parties on the morning of October 11, 2013. Zhang Supei, agent ad litem of Xinghe Company, and Song Xinyue and Jin Qiang, agents ad litem of Runde Company, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded upon examination.

Xinghe Company applied for reconsideration on the grounds that the second instance judgment erred in the application of law in determining the scope of protection of independent claims 2 and 6 of the patent in question. The main reasons are:

1. The Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases (Fa Shi [2009] No. 21) and the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law) clearly distinguish between the subject matter name and technical features using different legal terms, and emphasize that the scope of protection of a patent right is defined by the technical features. Therefore, the second instance judgment's determination that "the subject matter name, as a necessary content of the claim, has a limiting effect on its scope of protection" has no legal basis. 2. When Runde Company filed a request for invalidation of the patent in question, it submitted completely different comparative documents for claims 1, 2, and 6 respectively. When evaluating the inventiveness of claims 2 and 6, the Patent Reexamination Board did not consider the comparative documents submitted by Runde Company for claim 1, and when evaluating the inventiveness of claim 6, it also did not consider the comparative documents submitted by Runde Company for claim 2. Therefore, it can be inferred that the Patent Reexamination Board considered that the subject matter name is not a technical feature and is not a necessary technical means for solving the technical problem. 3. According to the specification and drawings of the patent in question, the composite of steel strip and plastic in step a of claim 2 includes two methods: one-step composite and two-step composite. During the patent application process, when Xinghe Company amended the text of the patent in question, it abandoned the two-step composite method and retained only the one-step composite method. According to the estoppel principle, the second instance court should not have included the two-step composite method within the scope of protection of the patent in question when making the infringement determination. 4. If the subject matter name of a method claim cites a preceding product claim, it should incorporate all the technical features of that product. When determining the scope of protection of claim 2, the second instance court mechanically believed that "the occurrence of a citation relationship to a preceding claim in the claims is to avoid unnecessary repetition of identical content between claims," which constitutes unclear fact-finding and erroneous application of law. 5. The citation relationship between independent claims is merely a formal difference in wording during the drafting of the patent application documents and is not a factor that must be considered when determining the scope of protection. 6. Claim 1 and claim 2 are not in a dependency relationship. Limiting the scope of protection of claim 2 by the technical features of claim 1 clearly violates the legal provision that "the scope of protection shall be determined by all the technical features stated in the claim." In summary, the second instance court's understanding of the scope of protection of claim 2 of the patent in question is erroneous. Similarly, the scope of protection of claim 6 of the patent in question is not limited by claims 1 and 2. Therefore, Xinghe Company requests the revocation of the second instance judgment and the maintenance of the first instance judgment according to law.

Runde Company argued in its defense that the facts found in the second instance judgment were clear, the application of law was accurate, and the outcome of the judgment was correct. The subject matter name is a necessary component of a claim, constitutes a necessary technical feature, plays an important role in clarifying the scope of protection of the patent right from the outset, and has a limiting effect on the scope of protection of the patent right. Therefore, Runde Company requests the maintenance of the second instance judgment and the dismissal of the application for reconsideration.

This Court finds upon examination that the specification and drawing 1 of the patent in question describe the one-step composite method of the method recorded in claim 2: A steel strip 9 from an unwinding device 1 is pulled by a traction machine 7, guided by a guide roller 2 into the composite die head 4, which is a key component for extrusion composite. The composite die head 4 is connected at a right angle to the extruder 3, and its internal cavity has a shape corresponding to the composite profiled strip 10. While the steel strip 9 passes through the composite die head 4, the plastic extruder 3 extrudes molten plastic into the composite die head 4. Inside the composite die head 4, the molten plastic wraps around the periphery of the steel strip 9, and under the traction force of the traction machine 7, it is pulled out from the composite die head 4, forming an unshaped composite profiled strip 10. The specification and drawing 2 also describe a two-step composite method, i.e., first forming a plastic profiled strip with open ribs, and then embedding the steel strip and sealing it. This technical solution is not recorded in the claims.

It is also found that the specification of the patent in question further states: In order to prevent the plastic between the reinforcing ribs from being pierced by sharp stone chips when the pipe is laid, the plastic shape between the two reinforcing ribs should not be a simple flat surface, but should have a shape with a middle protrusion.

This Court is of the opinion that the focus of this case is: 1. Whether the subject matter name has a limiting effect on the scope of protection of the patent right; 2. When a parallel independent claim cites a preceding independent claim, how should the limiting effect of the preceding independent claim on its scope of protection be determined.

1. Regarding the issue of whether the subject matter name has a limiting effect on the scope of protection of the patent right.

Article 59 of the Patent Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law) provides: "The scope of protection of the invention or utility model patent right shall be determined by the content of the claims. The description and drawings may be used to interpret the content of the claims." Article 21 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law provides that an independent claim for an invention or utility model shall include a preamble portion and a characterizing portion. The preamble portion shall state the subject matter name of the technical solution of the invention or utility model for which protection is sought and the necessary technical features common to the invention or utility model subject matter and the closest prior art. The characterizing portion shall state the technical features that distinguish the invention or utility model from the closest prior art, and these features, together with the features stated in the preamble portion, define the scope of protection sought for the invention or utility model. Therefore, under normal circumstances, when determining the scope of protection of a claim, the subject matter name recorded in the claim should be considered, and the actual limiting effect should depend on the impact that the subject matter name itself has on the subject matter for which protection is sought by the claim. In this case, when determining the scope of protection of claims 2 and 6, consideration should be given to the actual limiting effect that their subject matter names have on the subject matter itself for which protection is sought.

2. Regarding the issue of how to determine the limiting effect of the preceding independent claim on the scope of protection of a parallel independent claim when it cites the preceding independent claim.

Article 31, paragraph 1, of the Patent Law provides: "An application for an invention or utility model patent shall be limited to one invention or utility model. Two or more inventions or utility models belonging to a single general inventive concept may be filed as one application." Article 20 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law provides: "The claims shall contain independent claims and may contain dependent claims. An independent claim shall, from the whole, reflect the technical solution of the invention or utility model and record the necessary technical features for solving the technical problem. A dependent claim shall further limit the claim it refers to with additional technical features." Article 34 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law provides: "Two or more inventions or utility models belonging to a single general inventive concept that may be filed as one patent application in accordance with Article 31, paragraph 1, of the Patent Law shall be technically interrelated and contain one or more identical or corresponding specific technical features. The term 'specific technical features' refers to those technical features that define the contribution of each invention or utility model, as a whole, over the prior art." Section 2.2.1(2) of Part Two, Chapter Six of the Patent Examination Guidelines provides six permissible forms of drafting for claims of two or more inventions belonging to a single general inventive concept, including: independent claims for products or methods of the same category; independent claims for a product and a method of manufacturing the product; independent claims for a product and a use of the product; independent claims for a product, a method specially designed for manufacturing the product, and an apparatus specially designed for carrying out the method; independent claims for a method and an apparatus specially designed for carrying out the method.

Accordingly, in the claims of a patent application, there shall be at least one independent claim. When there are two or more independent claims, the claim written first is the first independent claim, and the other independent claims are parallel independent claims. An independent claim shall reflect the overall technical solution and determine the scope of protection of the patent right according to its own content. An independent claim may or may not have a citation relationship. When a parallel independent claim cites a preceding independent claim, the parallel independent claim remains an independent claim and is not a dependent claim. Although when determining the scope of protection of a parallel independent claim, the features of the cited independent claim should all be considered, they do not necessarily have a limiting effect on the parallel independent claim. Their actual limiting effect shall be determined based on whether they have a substantive impact on the technical solution or subject matter of protection of the parallel independent claim.

In this case, the first instance and second instance courts found that when compared with claim 1 of the patent in question, the accused infringing product of Runde Company lacked the two technical features of "the steel strip has several rectangular or circular through holes or the steel strip has rolled patterns on both sides" and "the plastic shape between the two reinforcing ribs has a middle protrusion." Both parties have no objection to this. Independent claim 2 of the patent in question records a method for manufacturing a steel strip reinforced plastic drainage pipe as described in claim 1, and its step a states: arranging the extruder and the composite die head at a right angle, introducing the steel strip from one end of the die head into the composite die head, and compounding it with plastic inside the die head, after cooling, shaping, and traction, forming a steel strip reinforced plastic composite profiled strip. Independent claim 6 of the patent in question records an apparatus for implementing the method of claim 2 for manufacturing a steel strip reinforced plastic drainage pipe, including a composite device for compounding the steel strip with plastic to form a profiled strip with steel strip reinforcing ribs. From the claims of the patent in question and the one-step composite method described in the specification, it can be seen that an ordinary steel strip, through the composite device recorded in claim 6 and step a recorded in claim 2, forms a composite profiled strip, i.e., the steel strip has rectangular or circular through holes or patterns, and the molten plastic generates a middle protrusion between the two reinforcing ribs. Although the claims and the specification do not provide specific structural descriptions of the device components for forming the through holes or patterns and the protrusion, based on the product technical features recorded in claim 1 of the patent in question, it can be inferred that the composite device recorded in claim 6 must necessarily have components that generate the above distinguishing features. Thus, the technical features recorded in claim 1 have a substantive impact on claims 2 and 6 and have a limiting effect. The accused infringing product lacks through holes or patterns and the protrusion, and Xinghe Company did not provide evidence to prove that the accused infringing apparatus has components for generating the above features. Therefore, it can be inferred that the accused infringing apparatus is different from the apparatus recorded in claim 6 and did not use the accused infringing method.

Given that the two-step composite method of step a of claim 2 of the patent in question is only described in the specification and drawings but not recorded in the claims, the patentee did not claim its inclusion within the scope of protection of the patent right, and the second instance court also did not include it within the scope of protection of the patent in question. This Court will not review this matter further.

In summary, the facts found in the second instance judgment are clear, and the application of law is correct. The grounds for reconsideration of Xinghe Company are untenable, and this Court does not support them. Xinghe Company's application for reconsideration does not meet the circumstances specified in Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. Pursuant to Article 204, paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, it is ruled as follows:

The application for reconsideration of Harbin Institute of Technology Xinghe Industrial Co., Ltd. is dismissed.
